g_h1:
Your first $10,000 in crypto.
Every step. Nothing at stake.
g_sub: Real life has no practice mode — this is it. Three apps, exactly like the real ones: a bank where your card lives, an exchange where you trade the top 250, and a self-custody wallet where the memes and the gas live. Real fees. Fake money.
g_disc: Free forever. Email sign-in, no password, no deposit — nothing to lose but bad habits.
g_bank_s: $10,000 lands on a virtual Visa. Move money to the exchange — and cash profits back out. Both directions cost a fee, like real life.
g_ex_s: A trading terminal: buy USDT, trade Bitcoin and 250 majors at live prices with a 0.1% fee. Custodial — they hold it for you.
g_wal_s: Addresses, a seed phrase, networks, gas in SOL — and 150+ live meme coins on 4 chains. Self-custody, the real thing.
g_l1: Fees are the curriculum. Card 1.8% in, 1% out, exchange 0.1%, DEX 0.3%, network fees $0.80-$8, gas per tx.
g_l2: Seed phrase moment. Shown once, never stored — exactly how self-custody works.
g_l3: Wrong network = lesson, not lost money. Try it here, never out there.
g_l4: Daily PnL, equity curve, average entries, realized profit and a full paper trail.

s1_c: Your $10,000 arrived on a virtual card in the BANK app. Link it to the exchange so you can buy crypto — you confirm it with the card’s last 4 digits.
s2_c: USDT is the dollar of crypto — it is what you trade with. Card purchases cost a 1.8% processing fee; in real life a bank transfer is cheaper.
s3_c: The exchange holds coins FOR you; a wallet is YOURS. You get real-looking addresses and a seed phrase — guard it with your life.
s4_c: Withdraw USDT from the exchange to your own address. Pick the network carefully — Solana costs $1, Ethereum $8.
s5_c: On-chain everything costs gas, and memes are paid for in the network’s coin. Swap some wallet USDT for SOL to unlock the degen zone.
s6_c: The setup is done — now trade. Bitcoin and the top 250 live on the exchange; the memes live in your wallet. Every fill shows its fee before you confirm.

dp_lesson: Crypto deposits arrive from your MarginPad Wallet (or from another trader) over the internal MarginPad Chain.
cd_p: Your exchange deposit addresses — one per network family. The easy way: open Wallet → Exchange → Send to the exchange and the address is filled in for you.

mc_p: To buy crypto you first link a payment method to an exchange. Confirm it is your card by typing the last 4 digits:
mc_lesson: Real-life lesson: only ever link cards on exchanges you trust, with 2FA on. If anyone asks for your FULL card number and CVV over chat — it is a scam.

mo_p: USDT is a stablecoin — 1 USDT stays worth ~$1. It is what you actually trade with. Card balance: {usd}
mo_lesson: Card purchases cost 1.8% here (real on-ramps charge 1.8-4%). A bank transfer is usually near-free — worth the wait for big amounts.
mo_ok: Done — {usd} USDT is on your exchange balance (fee {fee}).
mo_toast: USDT bought — the Exchange app is open for business.
mo_notlinked: Link the card to the exchange first.
mf_nothing: Nothing to cash out — everything is already on your card.
mf_p: Selling USDT back to dollars on your card — the way profits actually leave crypto. Exchange balance: {usd} USDT
mf_lesson: Cashing out costs 1% here (min $1). Real exchanges charge fiat-withdrawal fees too — and your bank may add its own. In and out, someone always takes a cut.
mf_toast: {usd} is back on your card. Full circle.
wc_p: Two very different exits. Pick where the money goes:
wc_fiat_s: Fiat withdrawal — sell USDT for dollars · 1% fee
wc_crypto_s: Crypto withdrawal — USDT moves on-chain · network fee $0.80-$8
wc_lesson: On a real exchange these are separate menus too: "Withdraw fiat" and "Withdraw crypto". Crypto sent to a wrong address or network is gone — fiat just takes a day and a fee.
mw_p: On an exchange, THEY hold your coins. A self-custody wallet (like Phantom or MetaMask) is yours alone — secured by a seed phrase. Whoever knows the phrase owns the money.
mw_seed: Write these 12 words down, in order. This is the ONLY backup of a real wallet. Shown once — never stored, never recoverable. Anyone who has it can take everything; no legit support will ever ask for it.
mw_evm: Your EVM address (Ethereum · Base · BNB Chain)
mw_ck: I wrote down my seed phrase and understand that in real life losing it means losing my money — and sharing it means losing it faster.
mw_toast: Wallet created. Next: send USDT to it from the exchange.
wd_need: You need USDT on the exchange first — buy some with your card.
wd_p: Moving coins from the exchange to YOUR wallet is a real on-chain transfer. You choose the network — the coins are the same, the fees are not. Exchange balance: {usd}
wd_ph: your wallet address for the chosen network
wd_hint: Your own address lives in the Wallet app → Receive. Always copy-paste it — never type an address by hand.
wd_lesson: The network on the exchange MUST match the network of the destination address. USDT sent over the wrong chain to the wrong address is gone forever. Here it is safe to get it wrong — try it.
wd_ok: Sent — {usd} USDT arrived in your wallet ({net} fee {fee}).
wd_toast: USDT is in your wallet. Next: swap some for SOL.
wd_badaddr: That address does not match the chosen network format.
wd_insuf: Not enough on the exchange (remember the network fee).

co_lesson: This is the real-world shape of a cash-out too: DEX → wallet → exchange → bank, a fee at every hop. That is why traders plan the exit before the entry.

sd_lesson: On a real chain a transfer is FINAL — no bank, no undo, no support line. Triple-check the address. Here, sending to an address that does not exist is refused (out there, the money would be gone).

rc_lesson: Real-life habit: copy-paste, send a tiny test amount first, and check the first + last 4 characters after pasting. Clipboard-hijack malware swaps addresses.
rc_copied: Address copied. Check the first and last 4 characters when you paste.

f_text: Demo life-simulation with practice funds — prices, fees, gas, networks and slippage mirror real markets but no real money is involved and nothing can be withdrawn. The bank, card, exchange, wallet, addresses and seed phrase are simulated for education. Not financial advice. · Try futures paper trading · Learn in the Academy
tm_e_thin_pool: The pool behind this token holds under $1,000 — a sale this size cannot fill. Real rugs look exactly like this.
tm_e_bad_pool: That pool prices a different token. Nothing was filled.
d2_p: Your Today PnL and the green-day calendar start counting at midnight UTC — the first full day draws tomorrow. Want one line a day about how your portfolio moved?
d2_on: Done — one line a day, only on days something moved.
d2_denied: Notifications are blocked in this browser — allow them in the site settings, or use Telegram.
d2_lesson: One message a day at most, and none on a flat day. Switch it off here any time.
rug_line: The pool behind this token holds {usd} — the liquidity was pulled. Selling would return almost nothing. This is what a rug looks like from the outside.
rug_stale: No live price for this token any more — the pool is gone or unreadable. Its last known value is shown.
